messages.content: We have the St. Louis spring-break dates settled: Sunday March 16 through Friday March 21, five nights. It will be the three of us. Forest Park is the focus, we have tickets for a Wednesday evening performance at the Fox, and we want one downtown day. I need to figure out whether flying from Dallas or driving makes more sense, where to stay, and what the whole framework costs.

I can compare it door to door rather than looking only at airfare. What flight price and schedule are you seeing, and would you rent a car in St. Louis? For the drive, I will assume you leave from home in Dallas unless there is another starting point.

Home in Dallas. The reasonable nonstop is about $248 each round trip. It leaves DFW at 9:10 Sunday morning and the return leaves St. Louis at 4:35 Friday. We would check one bag. I am not sure about renting a car; that is part of the question.

For three people, airfare starts at $744. Add roughly $70 for one checked bag round trip if the fare does not include it, plus about $108 for six calendar days of DFW parking. With a 25-minute drive to DFW, parking, security, the 1 hour 45 minute flight, and the trip from STL to the hotel, the outbound is about 5 to 5.5 hours door to door. Friday should be similar. A compact rental for five days is likely around $330-$390 after taxes, before hotel parking and fuel. Without a rental, airport rides and trip transportation can be estimated separately.
Now compare that with driving. We can take our own midsize SUV. I do not want an optimistic drive time that ignores stops.

Dallas to St. Louis is roughly 630 miles each way. The map time is around 9 hours, but for three people with fuel, meals, and two or three breaks, I would budget 10 to 10.5 hours each direction. At about 25 mpg, 1,260 highway miles uses roughly 50 gallons. At an estimated $3.05 per gallon, base fuel is about $153; allowing local driving brings fuel to about $175. There are no major toll costs on the straightforward route, though a small contingency is sensible. The real tradeoff is giving up most of Sunday and Friday versus saving several hundred dollars and having the SUV available all week.

Assume we would leave Dallas at 7:00 Sunday morning and could leave St. Louis after breakfast Friday. What does the flight cost with a rental, and what does it cost if we fly and use rideshares instead?

Using planning estimates: fly plus rental is $744 airfare, $70 bag, $108 DFW parking, $360 rental, about $25 rental fuel, and whatever the hotel charges for parking. Before hotel parking, that is about $1,307. Fly plus rideshares is $744 airfare, $70 bag, $108 DFW parking, about $90 total for airport transfers, and approximately $130-$180 for the Forest Park, Fox, and downtown movements. I would carry $1,167 as the midpoint. Driving is about $175 fuel plus hotel and downtown parking, so transportation itself is dramatically cheaper.

Let us work on hotels, because parking could change that. I see the Drury near Forest Park at $1,238 total for five nights with two queens, breakfast, and free parking. There is also a downtown hotel at $196 a night before tax, but it charges $35 a night to park. Would splitting three nights by Forest Park and two downtown make the sightseeing easier?

It would make the downtown day easier, but only one day benefits. A two-night downtown stay adds a hotel move, packing, checkout timing, and about $70 in parking. At roughly 17% tax, the downtown room would be about $459 for two nights before parking, or $529 with parking. If the Drury prorates near $248 per night all-in, three nights there would be about $743, putting the split lodging near $1,272. That is already about $34 above the five-night Drury total, and it does not price the inconvenience of moving.
The Wednesday performance is at 7:30. If we stay by Forest Park all five nights, are we creating a transportation problem for the Fox and downtown?

No. The Fox in Grand Center is only a few miles east of the Forest Park area. With your SUV, allow 15-25 minutes depending on traffic and about $15-$25 for event parking. Downtown is roughly another 10 minutes east; one day of garage parking near the Arch or City Museum should be budgeted at $25-$35. Those two parking charges are much less disruptive and less expensive than changing hotels.
What if we fly and do not rent a car? The Drury says it has a shuttle, but I cannot tell whether that means airport service or just something local.

I would not count on that shuttle until the hotel confirms its route, hours, and whether advance reservations are required. For comparison, assume paid airport transfers. The Forest Park museums can be grouped with walking and short rides, but the hotel-to-attraction distances vary, and March weather may make walking less appealing. The Fox trip and downtown day are manageable by rideshare. Flying without a car works, but it requires more coordination and leaves the local total somewhat variable.

Our daughter would rather have a separate sleeping space than share one room for five nights. I found a one-bedroom suite in Clayton for $1,515 total. Parking is $18 nightly, and breakfast is included. How should that compare with the Drury room?

For five nights, the Clayton suite becomes $1,605 after $90 parking. It gives you meaningful separation and still keeps Forest Park convenient, but it is $367 more than the Drury. Driving with the Drury produces a lodging-and-transport base of about $1,463: $1,238 hotel, $175 fuel, and roughly $50 for Fox and downtown parking. Driving with Clayton is about $1,830. The room configuration is therefore a $367 comfort decision, not a location requirement.
Please include food only where the hotel changes it. Both include breakfast, and I do not want a general meal estimate. Also, does the Drury evening food materially affect the comparison?

I will leave ordinary lunches and dinners out. If the Drury's evening reception is offered on all five dates and is substantial enough for your family, it could replace one or two casual dinners, but I would not assign savings until the current schedule and menu are verified. Treat it as potential upside rather than money needed to make the option fit.
Give me the complete side-by-side using the Drury for five nights. For the flight options, include hotel parking only if there is a rental. For driving, include the Fox and downtown parking.

Five nights at the Drury: driving is $1,238 lodging, $175 fuel, and $50 local parking, totaling about $1,463 before non-breakfast meals. Flying with a rental is $1,238 lodging, $744 airfare, $70 bag, $108 DFW parking, $360 rental, $25 rental fuel, and $50 local parking, totaling about $2,595. Flying with rideshares is $1,238 lodging, $744 airfare, $70 bag, $108 DFW parking, and about $245 for airport and local rides, totaling about $2,405. The rideshare number could move by roughly $50 with surge pricing or extra trips.
And in actual trip time, the flight saves about five hours each way, correct? I want to be sure I am not overstating it.

That is a fair estimate. Driving is about 10 to 10.5 hours each way with stops. Flying is around 5 to 5.5 hours door to door if the flight is on time, so the expected savings is about five hours each direction. On Sunday, flying gets you into the city around early afternoon instead of roughly 5:00-5:30 p.m. Driving Friday after breakfast gets you home around early evening; the 4:35 flight likely gets you home around 8:00 p.m. after collecting the bag and retrieving the car, so the flight is not clearly better on the return day despite less time in transit.
That makes driving look more practical than I expected. Is there any reason to split the hotel if we drive?

Not for this itinerary. Forest Park accounts for multiple days, the Fox is a short drive, and downtown needs only one parking session. The split costs slightly more, adds a move, and still requires the SUV for the rest of the trip. Its only material benefit is walking access during the downtown portion, which is too limited here to offset the disruption.

Then set the working framework as driving and all five nights near Forest Park. Do not reserve the hotel yet. I still need to discuss whether the separate bedroom is worth $367, so keep both lodging versions visible and state the budget difference clearly.

Working framework only, with nothing reserved: leave Dallas around 7:00 a.m. Sunday, drive approximately 10 to 10.5 hours including stops, and use one Forest Park-area base for all five nights. The value version is the Drury two-queen room at $1,238 including breakfast and parking; with $175 fuel and $50 for Fox and downtown parking, the trip base is about $1,463 before other meals and activities. The separate-space version is the Clayton one-bedroom suite at $1,515 plus $90 parking; with the same fuel and local parking, its base is about $1,830. The suite costs $367 more. A split stay is not recommended, and flying would add roughly $942 with rideshares or $1,132 with a rental compared with driving and staying at the Drury. Hotel availability, cancellation terms, suite bedding, and the Drury shuttle and evening-reception details still need live verification before any reservation.
